Section: Safar have been pioneers in cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and anesthesiologists. The practice of anesthesia has changed dramatically since the days of John Snow. The modern anesthesiologist must be both a perioperative consultant and a deliverer of care to patients. In general, anesthesiologists are responsible for nearly all “noncutting” aspects of the patient’s medical care in the immediate perioperative period. The “captain of the ship” doctrine, which held the surgeon responsible for every aspect of the patient’s perioperative care (including anesthesia), is no longer a valid notion when an anesthesiologist is present. The surgeon and anesthesiologist must function together as an effective team, and both are ultimately answerable to the patient rather than to each other. The modern practice of anesthesia is not confined to rendering patients insensible to pain (Table 1–1).
